To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

alcohol-related advertisements from Swedish women's magazines over the past few years have positioned women in a number of different subject positions that reflect the traditional norms of “the housewife contract” and “the equality contract” as well as a new “gender contract”.
alcohol-related advertisements in women's magazines from Sweden, Finland and Norway have repeatedly positioned women in gender-specific subject positions.

the alcohol-related subject positions in women's magazines have changed from the 196os to 2000s, and that the subject positions in the 1960's are more traditional, while the subject positions from 2000s are more modern.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how gender is made visible in women's magazine advertising.
how the gender system is reproduced in the private and public domains, and how the gender system and the drinking culture are interwoven.
how the gender system is reproduced and transformed in alcohol-related advertising.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the private and the public domains, as well as the gender system, are still very much in flux.
alcohol-related advertising has been used to promote the traditional gender system in both countries, although the ways in which it has been used have varied over the years.
the subject positions in alcohol-related advertisements have changed and shifted over the years, and that those changes have been related to the shifting border between the private and the public.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the subject positions appearing over time and in the various advertisements are not fixed but rather changeable and fluid.
the alcohol-related subject positions in the advertisements have changed, but not as much as one might think, and that the traditional gender roles and the private domain are still present.
women are not only positioned as objects of male desire in the advertisements, but also as objects of their own desire.
The main takeaway from our work is that
alcohol advertising in women's magazines has a strong potential for gendered socialization and normalization of alcohol use.
alcohol-related advertisements in women's magazines can be used as an important source of data in gender studies, and in particular in studies of gendered subject positions.
alcohol-related advertisements in women's magazines can be used to study the shifting borderline between private and public life.
